description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between a model’s accuracy and an underlying metric (likely a confidence or calibration score) ranging from 0.91 to 0.98, as presented in the paper “Feedback Friction: LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback.” The x-axis, labeled with values from 0.91 to 0.98 in increments of 0.01, appears to represent a continuous scalar input—possibly a threshold or confidence level—with a linear scale. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 and is also linear, indicating the proportion of correct predictions. Three distinct lines are plotted: a solid blue line with circle markers remains consistently high, hovering near 1.0 across the entire x-axis range, suggesting stable performance. An orange dashed line with diamond markers starts at approximately 0.65 at x=0.91, peaks near 0.92 at ~0.92, then steadily declines to ~0.08 by x=0.98. A green dash-dotted line with square markers begins near 0.2 at x=0.91, dips slightly to ~0.07 at x=0.92, then rises monotonically to ~0.90 by x=0.98. Error bars are present on all data points, indicating variability or uncertainty in the measurements, with larger error bars observed at the extremes of the x-axis for the orange and green lines. The plot visually contrasts the stability of the blue line with the opposing trends of the orange and green lines, suggesting different behavioral regimes or model responses under varying feedback or calibration conditions.
